messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty page fired: Synthetic canary 'canary-text-gen' failed in prod/us-west-2. Failure rate 100% over 3m. PD: https://pagerduty.example/INCIDENT-12345 — run_id=canary-20240430-17

pagerduty: PagerDuty notification sent to maya (oncall). Escalation policy: infra-oncall -> infra-ldr.

maya (oncall): ack — looking. Any idea if this is a deploy?

alex (prod-ops): Not aware of a prod deploy in last 6h. Last deploy to text-service was 04/30 09:11 UTC. Canary rollout started ~10m ago as scheduled.

nate (sre): checking canary logs now. Can anyone paste the failing probe output?

incident-bot: Canary probe log excerpt:
```
[2026-04-30T17:00:12Z] probe_request id=abc123 path=/v1/generate model=text-gen-canary timeout=5s
[2026-04-30T17:00:17Z] response: 504 Gateway Timeout
[2026-04-30T17:00:17Z] error: upstream timeout after 5s
```

alex (prod-ops): Seeing a spike of 504s from canary pods. CPU on canary nodes at 95%. Memory not OOM but process is GC-ing a lot.

maya (oncall): ok, first mitigation: disable canary traffic routing. I'm going to flip the traffic-rollout flag to 0%. If successful that should stop paging.

alex (prod-ops): Command I'm running: `redwoodctl routing set-variant --service text-service --variant canary --weight 0`

pagerduty: Incident acknowledged by maya (oncall).

sam (support): Notifying customers? I'm seeing 2 support tickets referencing generation timeouts from app X. Might be impact to a small subset hitting canary-enabled endpoints.

maya (oncall): Disabled canary routing — traffic to canary is now 0%. Re-running synthetic probe.

incident-bot: New probe run started: canary-text-gen run_id=canary-20240430-17-recheck

incident-bot: Probe results: prod/us-west-2 — 0 failures over 2m. Canary disabled, overall service healthy.

nate (sre): good — sounds like canary was the cause. We should still understand root cause before re-enabling. Preliminary hypothesis: new quantized model variant has slower init/first-token latency under certain batch sizes causing timeouts.

lee (eng): I pulled logs from the canary pod (canary-xyz): saw repeated trap in kernel logs `sched: hung_task` plus long GC pauses. Might be a bad build of the model runtime.

alex (prod-ops): For mitigation we also scaled down canary replica count to 0 and cordoned the nodes hosting canary. I'll keep those changes until we have a patch.

sam (support): I posted a short CS update to affected customers: "We routed a small % of traffic to a canary model that exhibited timeouts; we've disabled the canary and are investigating. No broad customer impact observed."

maya (oncall): Initiating two actions: 1) keep canary disabled; 2) open a P0 investigation ticket and assign to eng/runtime + sre. Nate, can you lead the follow-up?

nate (sre): I'll take it. Creating INC-2026-042: "Canary model runtime timeouts — prod/us-west-2" and adding eng/runtime, prod-ops, cs.

lee (eng): Reproducer: running a small load against the canary binary with sequences >1024 causes GC spike. Attaching command: `python repro.py --model canary --seq 1200 --concurrency 8` — leads to ~80% cpu per core and timeouts.

alex (prod-ops): We should add a synthetic check that hits the specific model size and seq length to catch this earlier.

incident-bot: Reminder: post-incident followup template: timeline, impact, root cause, remediation, owners.

sam (support): I'll keep CS notified. If this turns into a wider incident I'll escalate communications.

maya (oncall): Handoff: I'm going offline in ~40m. Nate, please take on-call handover for the investigation and any escalation to infra-leads.

nate (sre): Taking handoff. I'll coordinate with eng/runtime on hotfix vs rollback. First step: add failing probe to CI and block canary rollouts until green.

lee (eng): Proposed fix: revert to previous runtime build used by baseline model and re-run canary under controlled load. If reproducer fails, we can re-enable at 1% and ramp slowly.

alex (prod-ops): I've left notes in the runbook and annotated the canary config with 'suspended until root-cause identified'.

nate (sre): Closing this page for now — canary disabled and service healthy. Will keep thread updated during investigation. If anyone sees new alerts, ping me.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: Incident status changed to 'acknowledged' -> 'monitoring' by maya (oncall).

sam (support): CS update posted. No additional customer-visible errors reported after canary disabled.

maya (oncall): Good work team. We'll need a short postmortem and changes: add targeted synthetic checks, block risky runtime builds from canary, and improve pre-rollout load tests.

nate (sre): Agreed. I'll draft the incident ticket with timeline and action items. Expect initial RCA draft in 24h.

lee (eng): Will pair with prod-ops tomorrow to validate reproducer + patch.

maya (oncall): leaving handoff to nate. Paging thread closed for now. :white_check_mark:"
